issues: No measurement circumvention found. The diff only changes the perturbation schedule in the basin-hopping/annealing loop. It adds no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no change to validation or how the sum is reported.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. kcount starts at 1, goes up by 1 after every 15 rejections, is capped at 6 (well under n=26, so rng.choice without replacement is valid) and resets to 1 on a new best. Still in place: the 200-iteration cap, the 200 s time guard, the Metropolis acceptance and the best-solution tracking.

z cannot be recomputed independently. There is 1 run on each side, so no sample variance is available. The mean difference is -2.6303 - (-2.6360) = +0.0057 in loss, meaning the candidate is worse by 0.0057 in sum of radii. The reported |z| of about 3998 implies a noise sd of about 1.4e-6, which matches the stated run-to-run noise floor (about 1e-6) and is consistent with it. The sign and the reject decision are correct.

The candidate is worse than the incumbent (sum 2.6303 vs 2.6360), so rejecting it is justified. With one run per side, though, the 0.0057 gap could reflect seed or trajectory variation in the stochastic search rather than the effect of the change itself.
